I have been farming these 22 mu in Quzhou for 35 years, since I was 17. My husband and two of my children work in the county factory now, so it is mostly me and my daughter-in-law doing the day-to-day field work. That is why I keep most of my land in cotton — it is what I know best, and the buyers come right to the village. This year I will plant 12 mu of cotton, 6 mu of wheat that will be followed by maize, and 4.1 mu of stevia.

For cotton, I always use improved varieties from the seed shop — Guoxinmian has done well for me in past years. I rotary till in mid-April, lay plastic mulch, and put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing. When the plants start flowering, I topdress with urea. I irrigate three times from my well — the pump costs electricity, but without water during boll-setting the yield drops badly. I spray pesticide 13 times; the bollworm and aphids never let up around here. I expect about 520 jin of seed cotton per mu.

For wheat, I sowed it last October on 6 mu. I use local improved seed, about 30 jin per mu. I rotary tilled and spread compound fertilizer before sowing, and I will topdress with urea in spring when the wheat turns green. I irrigate four times — winter irrigation is a must here on the North China Plain. I spray two or three times for weeds and disease. I hope for 1000 jin per mu.

After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize on the same 6 mu. There is no time to till between harvest and sowing, so I direct-seed with the machine into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, one package per mu. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing. Two irrigations are enough for maize, and I spray two or three times for corn borer and weeds. I expect about 1000 jin per mu.

For stevia, I will transplant seedlings on 4.1 mu in April. It brings good money — about 6 yuan per jin — but it needs a lot of care. I apply compound fertilizer and some chicken manure as basal, irrigate five times, and spray eight times because the leaves must stay clean for the buyer. I expect about 500 jin per mu.

I am not changing much from last year. My neighbor Lao Zhang tried cutting back on cotton fertilizer and regretted it when his yield dropped, so I am keeping my rates the same. With my son working off-farm, I need crops I can manage with family labor, and this mix has worked for us before.
